feature: Guides at dead ends, and the gaps they record
description: Where hexa's path does not work, hexa prints a guide: what is inconsistent, the route around it that keeps the pipeline's guarantees, and where the fix in hexa belongs. Each guide printed records a hit; `hexa gap pr` turns a gap into a pull request body.

specs.description: Every guide in the table has an id, a what, at least one step around, and a fix naming a hexa path.
specs.then: Every id is unique kebab-case; what is non-empty; around has at least one step; fix names at least one path that exists in the hexa workspace.

specs.description: A guide is not a free-form message: an entry without a route around or a fix is refused.
specs.given: A Guide built with an empty around, and one with an empty fix.
specs.then: Both are rejected, each naming the missing field.

specs.description: `hexa spec draft` with no completion model reachable prints the no-completion-model guide.
specs.given: A project with an ADR, HOME pointing at an empty directory (no inference registered), no provider environment variables.
specs.then: It exits non-zero. Its output says no completion model is reachable before any transport error, and contains the guide's numbered steps and `hexa gap pr no-completion-model`.

specs.description: A guide never turns a failure into a success, and an ordinary error prints no guide.
specs.given: The state of S03; and separately `hexa spec draft <an id with no ADR file>` for an ADR that does not exist.
specs.then: S03's run still exits non-zero. The missing-ADR run exits non-zero and prints no `hexa gap pr`.

specs.description: Printing a guide appends one hit; `hexa gap list` ranks by hits.
specs.given: HOME at an empty directory; the S03 dead end reached twice from project A and once from project B.
specs.then: ~/.hexa/gaps.jsonl has three lines with id no-completion-model. The list shows no-completion-model with count 3 and last project B.

specs.description: Recording a gap reaches no network and writes nothing in the project.
specs.given: The S05 runs, with the network unreachable (HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY at a closed local port).
specs.when: The project trees are compared before and after.
specs.then: No file under either project changed; the runs behaved as with the network up.

specs.description: `hexa gap add` records an unlisted guide that `hexa gap list` shows.
specs.when: `hexa gap add guard-x --what "w" --around "step one" --fix hexa-cli/src/commands/spec_ledger.rs` then `hexa gap list` are run.
specs.then: The add exits 0; the list shows guard-x marked unlisted with its what.

specs.description: An unlisted guide needs a route and a fix, and may not reuse a listed id.
specs.when: `hexa gap add` is run without --around, without --fix, and with the id no-completion-model.
specs.then: All three exit non-zero, each naming why; gaps.jsonl has no new line.

specs.description: The CLAUDE.md template tells an agent to add a guide when it routes around hexa.
specs.then: It contains `hexa gap add` in the same section as "build the verb".

specs.description: `hexa gap pr` prints a title and a body with the hits, the route and the files.
specs.then: Stdout has a first line title, then a body containing the what, "3" hits, both project names, the around steps and every fix path.

specs.description: `hexa gap pr` opens nothing and changes nothing; an unknown id fails.
specs.given: The S05 state, inside a git repository.
specs.when: `hexa gap pr no-completion-model` and `hexa gap pr nope` are run.
specs.then: The first exits 0 with git status and gaps.jsonl unchanged. The second exits non-zero naming the unknown id.

specs.description: Every `hexa ` step in every guide is a real command.
specs.when: For each around step beginning `hexa `, the words before the first argument are run with --help.
specs.then: Each exits 0. The check counts at least one such step, so an empty table does not pass.

specs.description: The no-completion-model guide's `hexa spec accept` step passes the check.
specs.given: The no-completion-model guide and the built binary.
specs.when: The §6 check runs over its steps.
specs.then: `hexa spec accept --help` is run and exits 0, and the check reports that guide as passing.

specs.description: A guide naming a verb hexa lacks fails the check.
specs.given: A guide whose around step is `hexa no-such-verb`.
specs.then: It fails, naming the guide id and the step.

specs.description: The table starts with the three guides found building ADR-2610301330.
specs.then: They include no-completion-model, link-hand-written-tests and guard-test-is-a-mirror; link-hand-written-tests' steps end with `hexa spec seal`.

specs.description: A first guide's route keeps the pipeline's guarantee: the red commit is set only after the tests are committed failing.
specs.when: Its steps are read in order.
specs.then: The step committing the red tests comes before the step setting `red`, which comes before `hexa spec seal`; no step sets `red` to a commit named before the tests are run.
